title: Dark Factory: OpenClaw Ships Faster Than You Can Read the Diff — Vincent Koc, OpenClaw
talk_summary: A core maintainer of OpenClaw describes running a 'dark factory' of many parallel coding-agent sessions (swim lanes) to ship thousands of commits a day, arguing the bottleneck has shifted from tokens to human attention, taste, and process. He details concrete practices: swim-lane partitioning by work type, over-fitted AI-generated tests as a refactor safety net, skill files, PR dedup/semantic clustering, and synthetic-provider evals.

takeaways.what_they_do: Runs 5-20 parallel agent sessions split into lanes by category (CI/tests, features, bugs, P0/P1 triage), giving low-risk lanes autonomy and babysitting only high-risk ones.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I have swim lanes... CI to one side, you might have features on one side, you might have bugs on another.
takeaways.numbers: 5-20 swim lanes; ~15 foreground sessions, up to 60-70 agents with subagents

takeaways.technique: Over-fitted AI tests as refactor safety net
takeaways.what_they_do: Kept the AI-generated, over-fitted unit tests during a massive refactor; as long as they stayed green they had a rough signal the rewrite was close.
takeaways.evidence_quote: these awful sort of unit tests that AI code loves to generate that actually ended up over-fitting on our code... as long as they would go green, we knew we were kind of somewhat close
takeaways.numbers: 2,700 commits, ~1M lines changed, 82% of core codebase touched

takeaways.what_they_do: Maintains versioned 'dot skills' (e.g. technical-doc writing) and runs an agent over past session logs to propose improvements to the skill, then redeploys it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Go through the Codex sessions, read the logs, make improvements to the skill.

takeaways.what_they_do: Embeds and clusters incoming PRs/issues to dedupe and gauge pressure, using cluster size as a signal for what to prioritize.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have a way of kind of deduplicating and seeing what's out there... if there's enough pressure coming on one issue, it must be big enough
takeaways.numbers: one PR graph had 73,106 edges; project had ~60k PRs

takeaways.what_they_do: Built a fake Slack with synthetic and real models to run eval loops verifying each provider and channel works after refactors.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we decided to make a fake Slack of sorts with both synthetic models and real models, so we can run evaluation loops to check that each of the providers and the channels work

takeaways.what_they_do: Explicitly shifts from burning tokens to conserving them, treating human attention/compute as the real constraint and killing sessions that 'waffle'.
takeaways.evidence_quote: 2025 was about token maxing. 2026 is about not wasting them. It's about token efficiency.
